## Explore warmer, lower-price hours

Historical temperature and hourly electricity prices help put flexible heating
into context. Use the published zone prices when planning today's operation.
:::

```{r}
#| results: asis
site_metadata(snapshot)
if (is.null(snapshot$weather) || !nrow(snapshot$heatmap)) {
  cat('<p class="publication-note">Weather analysis is unavailable in this snapshot. ',
      'Use the East or West price page for electricity scheduling; a weather-inclusive ',
      'snapshot is needed for the heatmap.</p>')
}
```

## Temperature and electricity-price heatmap

```{r}
#| label: weather-price-heatmap
#| fig-height: 9
#| fig-alt: "Hourly temperature-band heatmaps for DK1 and DK2. Dark blue indicates the lowest observed mean consumer scenario price and white the highest."
plot_heatmap(snapshot)
```

Each tile is the snapshot's average consumer-scenario price for a one-degree
temperature band and a Copenhagen clock hour from **07:00 to 23:00**. Dark blue
marks the lowest observed mean price and white the highest. Missing cells mean
no matched observations; read the counts below before interpreting a pattern.

The heatmap uses the previous 30 completed days of available weather and prices,
joined by UTC timestamps. Check **provider** and **weather coverage** above for
the actual source, gaps and scenario. Weather from a historical model or
reanalysis describes modeled outdoor conditions, not a measurement at your house.

The **Radius / Andel scenario** is applied to both zones for comparison. DK1
cells are an illustrative use of those charges with DK1 spot prices; they do
not represent a western-Denmark customer's local grid tariff.

## Matched observations

```{r}
#| results: asis
cells <- snapshot$heatmap
if (nrow(cells)) cells <- cells[order(cells$PriceArea, cells$ConsumerPriceDKK), , drop = FALSE]
site_table(cells, "Temperature bands, hours, mean scenario prices and observation counts",
           "No weather / price observations were included in this snapshot.")
```

## What this tells you about a heat pump

This is a **weather and electricity-cost view**. It does not estimate heat
output, COP or a manufacturer's performance curve. Actual efficiency depends
on flow temperature, defrosting, building demand, controls and the installed
heat pump. Outdoor temperature alone cannot establish a cheapest heat-output hour.

Preserve comfort, hot-water requirements and your system's operating limits
when shifting use. The [DK2](east-denmark.qmd) and [DK1](west-denmark.qmd) pages
show the currently published wholesale windows.
